<reason>CON built the more durable case by anchoring the resolution to the realistic case (somatic self-regarding enhancement) and backing every claim with concrete legal analogs already in force—elective sterilization, kidney donation, breast augmentation, LASIK—showing consent already licenses grave, irreversible, non-therapeutic risk. PRO's opening had three pillars (irreversibility/germline, fictional consent, stable medical line), but the "fictional consent" pillar was never defended again after CON's rhinoplasty/beauty-industry rebuttal, and the "stable medical line" pillar was only partially defended (LASIK) while cosmetic surgery/implants went unanswered. PRO's case narrowed almost entirely to one argument—that a licensed somatic market will inevitably manufacture the infrastructure that dissolves any germline ban. That argument is plausible and PRO defended it cleverly in the final closing (flipping CON's opioid analogy to show normalization preceded enforcement), but it remains speculative causal prediction rather than a demonstrated mechanism, and CON explicitly forced PRO to carry that burden ("strict prohibition" is the affirmative ask) without PRO fully discharging it. CON's pressure questions (self-regarding consent principle, why not ban germline directly) were answered cleanly with A1:/A2: format; PRO's answers were largely reassertions of the infrastructure-creep claim. Both sides suffered a clipped-turn format cost (A's opening, B's rebuttal2), which roughly cancels out. On balance CON's broader, better-supported rebuttal coverage and cleaner burden framing edge out PRO's narrower, more speculative surviving argument.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 1 point that medicine already permits consent to grave, irreversible, non-therapeutic risk (elective sterilization, living kidney donation, cosmetic implants) directly gutted PRO's opening claim that "consent has never been sufficient" for such interventions, and PRO never returned to repair that pillar, leaving it effectively conceded for the rest of the debate.</best_rebuttal>
